subject: LLM load sprint kickoff & hands-on sync
messages:
From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@neonanalytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff & load sprint - availability and targets

Hi Jasmine / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the folks here at Neon want to move to a hands-on POC as the next step. We'd like to schedule a 3-part kickoff: a short intro (30m), a prompt routing & prompt-review workshop (60m), and then a focused load/benchmark window (2–3 hours) where we run representative traffic and validate throughput/latency.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm throughput target: aiming for sustained 1,200 tokens/sec across the app during peak-sim (we can provide traffic traces).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for single-turn generate calls (at the 90% traffic mix).
- Test harness: we use Locust + a lightweight prompt-replay harness; can you confirm Redwood can accept KV-cache warmup and prefix caching for the run?

We have availability next week (May 29–31) in the afternoons PT or the following week mornings PT. Please propose concrete slots and also include any pre-reqs (prompt sets, model variants, accounts).

Attaching a short scope doc and the harness spec.

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Cheng | Head of ML Ops, Neon Analytics
[Attachment: poc-scope-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 380KB)]
[Attachment: test-harness-spec.md (text/markdown, 12KB)]

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@neonanalytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & load sprint - availability and targets

Hi Alyssa — great to hear Neon is ready to go. Short answers up front: we can support KV-cache warmup and prefix caching, and we can run a sustained throughput target in your ballpark while instrumenting p50/p95. A few clarifying items so we size things correctly:

1) Workload mix: do you expect a 70/30 split of short (<64 tokens) to long (>=512 tokens) requests, or something different? That matters for kernel selection and batching.
2) Which model family do you want to test? We have benchmarks on the rdx-13b and rdx-70b quantized variants; rdx-13b will be cheaper but the latency profile differs.
3) Are you bringing your own data for prefix caching or will Redwood seed the cache from a golden prompt set you provide?

Proposed schedule (all PT):
- Tue May 30, 13:00–13:30 — Kickoff (Jasmine + Alyssa + Aditya)
- Tue May 30, 13:30–14:30 — Prompt routing & prompt review (hands-on, include CS & ML Ops)
- Wed May 31, 10:00–13:00 — Load + benchmark window (dry run first 30m, then 2-hour sustained run)

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short runbook with the pre-req checklist (prompt sets, sample traces, model pin). For the load window we’ll want admin access to your harness (or we can attach our runner to your Locust master).

Two small asks: please share a representative token-length histogram and confirm the model family. Also, can your procurement contact (procurement@neonanalytics.com) confirm if we should create a temporary dedicated project for the POC?

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[signature: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198]

From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@neonanalytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@neonanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & load sprint - availability and targets

Thanks Jasmine — that schedule looks good. A couple of clarifications:

- Workload mix: closer to 60/40 short/long; long requests are ~600 tokens on average (we'll attach the histogram).
- Model: let's start with rdx-13b-quant as the baseline. If latency is too high under load, we can try rdx-6b-ss on the fallbacks.
- Procurement: confirmed — we prefer a temporary dedicated project with isolated logs; procurement will send any paperwork next week.

We can host the Locust master (we'll provide the master endpoint and an access token). Please include your recommended batch sizes and any specific warmup sequence you'd like us to run before the main window.

I've attached the token histogram and a brief internal run outline. Also, can you add Monica from CS to the prompt-review session? She's looped here.

Alyssa

Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & load sprint - availability and targets

Perfect — confirmed. I booked the slots and shared a calendar invite with the runbook and pre-req checklist. Summary / next steps:

- Calendar:
  • Tue 2028-05-30 13:00–14:30 PT — Kickoff + prompt review (Google Calendar invite sent)
  • Wed 2028-05-31 10:00–13:00 PT — Load & benchmark window (dry run 10:00–10:30)
- Model: rdx-13b-quant pinned for the main run; fallback to rdx-6b-ss if we hit capacity cliffs.
- Throughput target: target sustained 1,200 tokens/sec (we'll measure token emit rate and per-request latency).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms; we'll generate a quality/latency dashboard during the run so we can see regressions live.
- Test harness: we will attach our runner to your Locust master — please send the endpoint and temp access token before Tuesday EOD.
- Pre-reqs you should provide by Monday EOD: token histogram (received), golden prompt set (JSONL), and Locust master URL + token.

Attachments included: runbook_link and quick-warmup.sh (stubs).

If anything changes we can pivot — otherwise see you Tuesday.

Cheers,
Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
